Next week totals about 40 mi (6+9+5+4+16), slightly under this week's 42, so it starts the taper sensibly. The 16-mile long run with the last 6 at marathon pace is a reasonable dress rehearsal two weeks out. Marathon pace near 8:35/mi matches her 3:45 goal. The week keeps her schedule (Monday and Friday off, session Wednesday, long run Sunday), and each day can be run as written. No must-never rule is broken. It falls short of a 5 for two reasons. It barely speaks to her anxiety, and it never tells her that one 20 is enough, which is the reassurance she needs. And calling this the "final build week" sits oddly with what is really the start of a taper.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You nailed the week as planned, and with the race on Sun Oct 18 we're done chasing distance. …
Answers: No, skip the 22-miler. Sun Oct 4 sits 14 days before the race, and the long run that close has to leave you fresh, not drain you.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off to open the final build week fresh.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, relaxed. Flush the long run out of the legs.
Wed: quality, 9 mi total with 2 mi easy, then 4 mi at marathon pace near 8:35/mi, then 3…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Recovery between the two pace days.
Fri: rest. Protects Sunday's dress rehearsal.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, conversational pace. Opens the legs for the long run.
Sun: long, 16 mi with first 10 easy near 9:50/mi, then last 6 at marathon pace near…
